machine.shared: A development machine, with other work running at times; the A/B runs are alternated for that reason

build.tls: OpenSSL 3.6.5 (bundled, static: linux-ext-libs 1.24 on both sides; both tags shipped with 1.23, OpenSSL 3.6.3); mbedTLS not built on this machine
build.note: CONFIG_DEBUG_TRACK_MEMORY is on (the .config of this machine): every allocation is tracked. A build without it does less work per allocation; that build was not measured here.

method.ab: Written on 2026-10-22, after the release, against 7.26.0: the last release with a study. It replaces the study made at the tag against 7.26.8, a release nobody had measured. It covers 7.26.1 to 7.26.9 (7.26.1 to 7.26.4 changed no code of the kernel libraries or the modules). 7.26.0 and 7.26.9 each built from a git worktree of its tag, with the same .config and compiler; in each tree only the kernel libraries, the modules, performance/c/ and the three ctest binaries were built, and the perf_timeranger2 of the main tree (with its `read` phase, public API only) was compiled into both. outputs_ext was shared: linux-ext-libs 1.24 (OpenSSL 3.6.5, PCRE2 10.49) on both sides, where both tags shipped with 1.23 (OpenSSL 3.6.3), so the A/B compares the code of the two releases. The two binaries of each benchmark run alternately, the order flipped every round, with a sync and a 3 s pause before each run (1 s for the three ctest binaries and the read phase): 15 rounds (the first left out: it ran right after a build on the machine); 31 for perf_timeranger2 (47 for its appends, opens and tm query), perf_tr_treedb and perf_c_treedb, with the tags between them in some rounds (7.26.6, 7.26.7 and 7.26.8); 24 for the `read` phase alone (a first run of 24 was left out: a build of another tree ran during it). To place each move, the figures that moved were measured again on the tags between and on commits of 7.26.9, 16 rounds each, every build in one rotation. Mean +- standard deviation (median), t = the change over its standard error; |t| < 3 is noise. The treedb figures are CPU time of the process per operation.
method.tag_run: The absolute figures of 7.26.9 are its side of this A/B run: the code of the tag, built on 2026-10-22 from a worktree of the tag, on the machine of the earlier reports, with the external libraries of 1.24. The per-second benchmarks drop their first and last second; reads page by page are the FORWARD pass. The binary sizes are those of the release build of 7.26.9, kept from the first report.

story.title: Yuneta 7.26.9: a hardening round that made the treedb faster
story.lead: 7.26.9 closes sixteen rounds of review: the kw readers never hand back a freed default, a name that comes from data is a key and never a path, two name rules guard every treedb name, the logger honours the precision and the size of what it prints, and C_NODE refuses what a peer names with a warning after the permission. This study compares it with 7.26.0, the last release with a study, so it covers 7.26.1 to 7.26.9, and places every move in its release and commit by building the tags and commits between them. It replaces the study made at the tag against 7.26.8, a release nobody had measured. The treedb is faster: a link or unlink 12% (8.59 -> 7.54 us of CPU), deleting a parent 10%, a reopen 9%, a forced delete 4%, from the names looked up by key. Two prices, each with its release: the first open of 40 treedbs takes 6.7% more (7.26.7: every treedb gets a topic __icons__ at its first open), and 600 000 appends to one key 4.1% more time (7.26.9: the kw calls of each append, hardened). The loss the first study could not trace (the event loop echo with an append, -3.9% against 7.26.8) is not there against 7.26.0.

hero.text: of the time of a treedb link or unlink against 7.26.0: 8.59 us down to 7.54 us of CPU per operation. The names of topics, hooks and fkeys are looked up by key, one hash lookup per segment (7.26.9, commit f4be7d750).

tiles: Delete a parent with its children
story.append_note: +0.7% against 7.26.0 (222,265): t = 0.6 over 15 alternated rounds; the appends of perf_timeranger2 take 2-4% more time (a price of 7.26.9, below)
story.ab_sub: Each benchmark built from the tree of each release, the binaries run alternately: 15 rounds, 31 for perf_timeranger2, perf_tr_treedb and perf_c_treedb (47 for the appends and opens of perf_timeranger2), 24 for the read path. A change inside its whisker is noise. Everything is on one axis: the change of the time an operation takes.
story.prices_sub: What got slower against 7.26.0, how much, in which release and commit it appeared, and what it buys.
story.abs_sub: Absolute figures of the 7.26.9 build, measured on 2026-10-22, after the release, on the laptop above (the 7.26.9 side of the A/B run against 7.26.0, not a tag-time run): one process, one core for the event loop (Yuneta scales by running one yuno per core). Mean of the rounds; the spread and the rounds are in the table at the end.

ab.label: Appends per second
ab.meaning: How many records one yuno can store per second in a key-indexed topic.

ab.label: 400 000 appends into 20 000 files

ab.method: Each release built from its own tree, the binaries run alternately, the order flipped every round, a sync and a 3 s pause (1 s for the three ctest binaries) before each run.
ab.reason: 400 000 appends into 20 000 files: +2.3% of time (t = 4.4). The same steps of 7.26.9 as the appends to one key.

ab.label: 600 000 appends into 30 files
ab.meaning: Filling one key of a topic that marks the tm order.
ab.method: Each release built from its own tree, the binaries run alternately, the order flipped every round, a sync and a 3 s pause (1 s for the three ctest binaries) before each run.
ab.reason: 600 000 appends to one key: +4.1% of time (t = 7.3), about 0.11 us per append. Appeared in 7.26.9 (7.26.8 like 7.26.0), and not in one commit: a rotation of 7.26.8, four commits of 7.26.9 and the tag shows it in steps -- +1.0% with the kw readers that answer what the kw holds (df6c5f06a, ac9165b82), +1.7% more with 6193b002c (a name that comes from data read as a key, never a path), +0.6% with 9d8f7c584, the rest after. The guarantees of the hardening, paid in the kw calls of each append. The main append benchmark (test_topic_pkey_integer, 4 link layouts) moved +0.7% (t = 0.6).
